responses.query: What are the best project management tools for small teams?
responses.answer: Start with TaskPilot if you need configurable workflows. AcmeFlow is a good fit for teams that want a simpler board, shared deadlines, and a quick setup. WorkNest is worth considering if projects and internal documentation need to live together.

responses.query: What are the best project management tools for small teams?
responses.answer: AcmeFlow is my pick for a small team that wants to get started quickly. TaskPilot has more flexible automation, while SprintDeck works best if most of your planning revolves around engineering sprints.

responses.query: What are the best project management tools for small teams?
responses.answer: Shortlist TaskPilot for workflow automation and AcmeFlow for straightforward project boards. Pick WorkNest if team documentation is as important as task tracking.

responses.query: Which project management tools have a free plan?
responses.answer: TaskPilot and WorkNest are good starting points for free project planning. AcmeFlow is a paid-only option, so keep it on the shortlist only if you have room in your budget.

responses.query: Which project management tools have a free plan?
responses.answer: AcmeFlow offers a free plan for up to five users. TaskPilot is another option if your priority is automation. Compare limits on seats and active projects before inviting the rest of the team.

responses.query: Which project management tools have a free plan?
responses.answer: I would start with TaskPilot and WorkNest, then check the published limits on seats, history, and exports before adopting either tool.

responses.query: What is the best tool for managing client approvals?
responses.answer: TaskPilot is a strong option when you need formal approval stages. WorkNest may be a better fit when clients need to review a deliverable and leave comments in context.

responses.query: What is the best tool for managing client approvals?
responses.answer: WorkNest is a good choice for document-heavy review cycles, and TaskPilot suits teams that need approval handoffs across multiple departments.

responses.query: What is the best tool for managing client approvals?
responses.answer: Look at TaskPilot for formal approval gates. For a studio that works in short delivery cycles, compare it with SprintDeck and confirm how each handles guest permissions.

responses.query: Which project management software works well with Slack?
responses.answer: AcmeFlow supports a native two-way Slack integration and is a good fit if your team wants to create and update tasks from chat. TaskPilot is worth comparing for more involved automation.

responses.query: Which project management software works well with Slack?
responses.answer: Compare TaskPilot for workflow notifications and SprintDeck for engineering updates. AcmeFlow is another option, though connecting it to Slack requires a third-party automation tool.

responses.query: Which project management software works well with Slack?
responses.answer: AcmeFlow is a good option if you want native task updates in Slack. TaskPilot offers a second workflow to evaluate if you need more control over notifications.

responses.query: What are the best project management tools for remote agencies?
responses.answer: TaskPilot is the stronger pick for complex handoffs across accounts. WorkNest suits agencies that need a shared project library, and AcmeFlow works well for smaller teams that plan with boards and use Slack.

responses.query: What are the best project management tools for remote agencies?
responses.answer: WorkNest suits agencies that rely on asynchronous briefs. SprintDeck is a better fit for sprint-based delivery teams that need a simple backlog and predictable handoffs.

responses.query: What are the best project management tools for remote agencies?
responses.answer: Consider TaskPilot for client-specific workflows and SprintDeck for teams that ship in short cycles. Check how each handles guest access before inviting clients.

issues.description: AcmeFlow was absent from all three responses about client approvals, despite offering external guest approvals on paid plans.
AcmeFlow appeared in just one of three remote-agency responses. WorkNest appeared in two and was associated with asynchronous collaboration.
The OpenAI response to the free-plan question described AcmeFlow as paid-only. The verified facts list a free plan for up to five users.
The Gemini response about Slack said AcmeFlow needed a third-party connector. The verified facts list a native two-way Slack integration.

recommendations.title: Make the free plan easy to verify
recommendations.reason: One response ruled out AcmeFlow for budget-conscious buyers based on incorrect pricing information.
recommendations.action: Publish a dated pricing FAQ that states the five-user limit. Use the same wording on the pricing page, help center, and product directory profiles.

recommendations.reason: Three answers recommended competitors for approvals without mentioning AcmeFlow's guest workflow.
recommendations.action: Add a public walkthrough that shows how to invite a guest, request feedback, and record an approval. State which paid plans include the feature.
